question: May app_install run from a stock modlib constructor launched by the system shell?
prototype_hypothesis: app_install must execute in the miwear/UI process because its registration path signals the miwear libuv loop through process-local descriptors
callsite_evidence: the device crash occurs in task 137, command 'system -c insmod', while the native Manager constructor is inside app_install sub_CA519AC
the crashing backtrace is app_install 0x0CA51AEC -> lvx_eventbus_send_with_cb 0x0CA28D28 -> libuv async sender sub_C2CB39C 0x0C2CB40E
libuv asserts at ../../apps/system/libuv/libuv/src/unix/async.c:213 because its one-byte wakeup write does not return exactly one byte
the async sender obtains the wakeup descriptor from the global loop object at loop+364; the crash stack records descriptor value 0xD5 while the current process is system rather than miwear
control_flow_evidence: app_install emits an event through the LVX eventbus after copying and linking the app descriptor
lvx_eventbus_send_with_cb queues an event and calls the libuv async sender
the libuv sender retries EINTR, accepts EAGAIN, and asserts for every other short/error result
the assertion is followed by rtc_watchdog reset, so constructor-thread registration is dynamically disproven
ownership_analysis: The resident descriptor and callback storage remain valid, but execution context is part of the ABI: fixed-address UI APIs are not safely callable merely because their addresses and layouts are correct. The Manager bootstrap must enter from miwear or be explicitly marshalled onto its event loop.
unsafe_assumptions: the exact errno returned by the failed wakeup write was not printed
successful app/page/launcher/notification behavior in miwear context still requires the next device probe
recommended_probe: Link the exact-target Manager code into the resident supervisor. Stage the GIF from Lua, then send legacy INSTALL through /dev/canopus. The synchronous device write callback executes in the calling watchface/miwear process and invokes app_install there. Keep CPC2 third-party package staging fail-closed.
